answer: The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so anyone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The atlas assignment is published and juniper records each panel. Shards are assigned from the umber graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 2239 identities would post 2864 proofs and burn roughly 67 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
